requirement:
> `Pass the UUID from next to read the next page in the same format. When next
> is absent, this is the last page.`
rationale:
structural: The requirement text is only the description string of the page-reading MCP tool: "Pass the UUID from next to read the next page in the same format. When next is absent, this is the last page." It prescribes no library, algorithm, signature, type, field or delegation through a named interface. The only obligation is that the tool advertises this exact text. That is a behavioral output obligation, not a structural one.

The supplied root already supplies it. `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tools.rs#impl[GraphSession<'_, '_, D>/Conversation]/fn[tools]` builds the `get_next_page` tool definition. Its description is identical to the required text, and it takes a `uuid` string parameter. No other root is needed, and the root carries the `{impl}` marker.

behavioral: The requirement fixes one observable obligation: the published `get_next_page` tool's description is exactly "Pass the UUID from next to read the next page in the same format. When next is absent, this is the last page." `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[published_tool_descriptions_match_the_contract]` is marked `{test}` for it. The test builds a `ValidationContext` with a scripted agent and calls `ask::<bool>()`. It then finds the `get_next_page` tool definition in the captured request and uses `assert_eq!` to compare its `description` with that exact string. A changed or missing description would fail the test, so the obligation is covered. `fn[default_tool_accepts_scalar_results_and_keeps_the_exact_prefix]` also checks the tool's name and parameter schema. That falls under the parent requirement `requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.pages.mcp`, not this one. No gaps found.
